question.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal.
question.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{2\cdot 1+1\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{2\cdot 2+1\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -4 \\ -8 \\ 4\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -3 \\ -7 \\ 5\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(2-\frac{9}{4})}^{2}+{(1-(-\frac{3}{4}))}^{2}+{(-3-(-\frac{7}{4}))}^{2}+{(1-\frac{5}{4})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{16}+\frac{49}{16}+\frac{25}{16}+\frac{1}{16}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{76}{16}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{19}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
